# Python Analysis

The Python Analysis layer is responsible for analyzing and verifying Python source code within your project.

## Key components

| File | Purpose | Main definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`src/analyze.js`](../src/analyze.js) | Analyzes lines of code to determine per-line facts. | `analyzeLines`, `lineStarts`, `matchToken`, `splitLines`, `lineIndexAt`, `baseInfo` |
| [`src/python-helper.py`](../src/python-helper.py) | Analyzes and verifies Python source for Docturnal. | `analyze`, `dump`, `env_names`, `verify`, `main`, `_dotted` |
| [`src/python.js`](../src/python.js) | Runs src/python-helper.py with python3 to analyze and verify Python source. | `analyzePython`, `findPython`, `pythonEnvNames`, `verifyPython`, `runHelper` |

## How it works

- **python-helper.py**: This Python script analyzes and verifies Python source code for Docturnal. It defines functions such as `analyze`, `dump`, `env_names`, `verify`, `main`, and `_dotted` to perform the analysis and verification.
- **python.js**: This script runs `python-helper.py` with `python3` to analyze and verify Python source code. It defines functions like `analyzePython`, `findPython`, `pythonEnvNames`, `verifyPython`, and `runHelper` to execute the analysis and verification scripts.
